stemMd: Across a period from left to right, atomic radius generally decreases. Which explanation is most appropriate?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Every atom loses all its neutrons.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Each successive element gains a completely new outer shell.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The number of protons decreases steadily.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Increasing nuclear charge attracts electrons within the same principal shell more strongly.

explanationMd: Across a period, proton number increases while added valence electrons occupy the same principal shell. Shielding does not fully offset the increased nuclear attraction, so the electron cloud generally contracts. The word “generally” acknowledges that periodic trends are not a substitute for every measured detail.

distractorRationale.d: Proton number increases across a period.
distractorRationale.c: New principal shells are associated with moving to a new period.
distractorRationale.a: Electron charge does not change across the periodic table.
distractorRationale.b: Neutron loss is not the basis of the periodic radius trend.
